title: Frisket template
description: The shape of a template, generated from the model rather than written beside it. It carries structure only: what is required of a section beyond its shape - alternative text on a figure, rows of equal width, columns asked of a container that places its children by coordinates - is checked by TemplateValidator, in the engine and in the designer, and cannot be expressed here. A template this schema accepts may still have things to report.

AdvancedTextItem.description: A paragraph of runs, each with its own style - what a plain TextItem cannot say, since it carries exactly one TextStyle for its whole string. Wrapping and pagination both work at the level of a whole *line*, built from pieces of one or more runs, not at the level of a run - see LayoutResolver.FlowAdvancedText.

$type.description: What kind of element this is.

Bookmark.description: Puts an entry in the document's outline, pointing at wherever this item lands. Null for none. Tokens are filled from the data like any text, so a group heading reading {Customer.Name} gives one bookmark per customer - which is what makes a file holding two hundred invoices usable at all.

BookmarkLevel.description: How deep the entry sits: zero at the top, one nested under the last entry above it at zero, and so on. A level that skips a step is pulled back to one more than its predecessor, since an outline with a hole in it is not a tree.

Language.description: The language of this element and everything under it, as a BCP 47 tag ("de-DE", "fr"). Null - the usual case - means the file's, which is Report.Language. PDF/UA 7.2 asks that a passage in a language other than the document's be marked as such, because a reader announcing German words with English phonemes is not a cosmetic fault: it is unintelligible. It reaches the file as /Lang on this element's structure entry, which is where PDF puts it, and costs nothing when it says the same as the file.

Role.description: What this element is, for a reader that cannot see it. Declared rather than guessed; see PdfRole.

AltText.description: What to say in place of something that cannot be read - a logo, a barcode, a chart. Without it such an element is announced as nothing at all, which is worse than the picture being missing: the reader is not told anything is there.

ShowWhen.description: A path in the data. The item is dropped - Visibility.Gone, so it takes no room and nothing beneath it moves - unless the value at that path is worth showing: present, and not an empty string, not zero, not false. Wanted the first time a form was reproduced faithfully. A box that only a credit note fills, a label for a number that is not always there, a line under an address line that may not exist: without this the choice is a rule drawn through empty space or a template per case.

HideWhen.description: The other way round: dropped when the value is there. Both may be given, and either one hiding the item is enough.

Style.description: Where the item sits and how much room it takes: position and size, margin and padding, size bounds, visibility, page breaks and alignment.

Runs.description: The paragraph's pieces, in reading order, each with its own style over the paragraph's.

Font.description: The paragraph's own style: family, size, alignment, line spacing. A run overrides pieces of this the way this overrides Report.DefaultFont.

BackPage.description: What is printed on the back of a sheet - conditions of sale, most often. It holds ordinary items, so it can be typed text with {tokens}, an image of a page, or any mix. It is laid out on a full page of its own: no header, no footer and no page band, because a back is not part of the document's flow.

Content.description: The content itself. Laid out over the whole sheet.

Scope.description: Which pages get a back: EveryPage, or the LastPage alone.

Padding.description: Margins of the back sheet, independent of the document's: conditions of sale are usually set closer to the edge than an invoice, being smaller print.

Backdrop.description: A picture behind every page: letterhead, pre-printed stationery, a tinted panel. A sibling of Watermark, deliberately not a mode of it. A mark says something about the document's standing - DRAFT, COPY - and is drawn to be hard to remove; a backdrop is the paper. One type covering both would have to mean "a word or a picture, a warning or stationery", which is the vocabulary trap section 16 of CLAUDE.md records, and its properties would then be half-meaningless either way.

Source.description: The picture. Nothing is drawn while it carries no bytes.

Area.description: Sheet by default, because stationery runs under the margins too.

NaturalWidth.description: Natural width in millimeters, NaN when unknown. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

NaturalHeight.description: Natural height in millimeters, NaN when unknown. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Scaling.description: How the picture sits in its rectangle. ImageScaling.Stretch here rather than the type's own ImageScaling.Uniform: filling the page is the plain reading of a background, and stationery is drawn at the paper's proportions already.

AlignHorizontal.description: Where it sits across its rectangle when it does not fill it - which is only ever the case under ImageScaling.Uniform or ImageScaling.None. Centred by default: a picture smaller than the sheet belongs in the middle of it. ItemAlign rather than a placement enum of its own. Nine named positions would be one vocabulary more to keep in step with a model that already says Start, Center and End on both axes - and section 5d is about exactly the property invented beside the one that was already there.

AlignVertical.description: Where it sits down its rectangle. Centred, for the same reason.

Opacity.description: 0 to 1. Full strength by default, which is right for stationery meant to be printed on and wrong for a photograph. Fade it here rather than in an image editor: a PNG carrying an alpha channel is refused outright by the PDF backend, so an author has no other way to do it. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

PageScope.description: Pages that carry it. All of them, unless narrowed.

BarcodeItem.description: A barcode. Its value goes through the same token and data binding as any text, so a template can carry {InvoiceNumber} and the data decides what is encoded. It is drawn as a grid of rectangles rather than as an image: it stays sharp at any size, costs a few hundred bytes instead of a bitmap, and needs nothing of a backend beyond the rectangle it already draws.

$type.description: What kind of element this is.

Value.description: What to encode. Tokens are substituted before it is read.

Correction.description: QR only: how much damage the code can take and still read.

Ink.description: The bars themselves. Black unless a section wants otherwise.

QuietZone.description: The margin of clear space around the code, in modules. Zero takes what the symbology asks for, which is not the same number: four for QR, ten each side for Code 128. A code set too close to a rule or to the edge of the page is a code a scanner refuses, and the fault looks like the printer's rather than the document's.

ShowText.description: Code 128 only: print the value underneath. Worth keeping - it is the eye's fallback exactly when a scanner will not read, which is when someone has to type the number in.

Font.description: How the value is printed under a linear barcode.

BaseItem.description: Anything a template can put on a page. Every element is one of these, and what it declares here is what they all have in common whatever their kind: where the item sits and how it looks (Style), what it is for a reader who cannot see it (Role, AltText), whether it earns its place at all (ShowWhen, HideWhen), and where it lands in the outline (Bookmark).

Body.description: The band between the header and the footer, and the part of a section that flows from one page to the next. Flowing is Layout being Stack, which Body sets for itself in its constructor. Set it to Absolute and the section comes out one page however much is in it: the children are arranged at their coordinates on that single page, whatever falls below the band is drawn off the sheet, and no further page is opened and no issue raised.

Layout.description: Always written, never inferred from its absence. The property starts at LayoutMode.Absolute, and the four containers that have to flow set themselves to LayoutMode.Stack in their constructors: Body, TableItem, ImageGridItem and SubTemplateItem. A Header, a Footer, a Section and a plain group keep the default. That matters because an absolute container hands every child the same box rather than taking room away as it goes, and a child that states no position of its own fills all of it - so two children of a band that says nothing land exactly on top of one another.

ColumnCount.description: How many columns the children flow into. One by default. Named ColumnCount rather than Columns because a table already has Columns, meaning its list of column widths - and a table is a container. Two different things under one name on the same inheritance chain is a fault waiting for somebody to write the wrong one; the compiler said so and the name changed. Only meaningful in LayoutMode.Stack: absolute children are placed by their own coordinates, and there is nothing for a column to decide.

ColumnGap.description: Millimetres between one column and the next. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

BalanceColumns.description: Whether the last page of a column flow is evened out. On by default. Columns fill in order, so the page where the text runs out has its first column full and its last nearly empty, which looks like a mistake. Balancing finds the shallowest height that still holds everything and uses that, so the columns end together. It costs a handful of extra passes over that page alone - pages that overflow have no spare room and are left as they are. Turn it off for a column of items that must start at the very top whatever happens.

RepeatOver.description: Name of the collection in the data this container repeats over, such as "Lines". The binder stamps its children out once per record; until it runs the container is an ordinary one holding the prototype. In a TableItem the header rows stay put and the remaining rows are the prototypes, cycled - two of them give banded rows for free. In any other container the whole set of children is one prototype block.

EmptyText.description: Shown in place of the children when the collection turns out empty.

GroupBy.description: Groups the collection by the value of this field before repeating, when the data arrives flat. Each pass then sees a synthetic record carrying Key, Count, a Sum of every numeric field - the subtotals - and the rows themselves under ContainerItem.GroupItems, ready for a nested repeat. Leave it null when the data is already grouped.

GroupItems.description: Name the grouped rows are published under. Defaults to "Items".

Childs.description: What this holds, in order. In a stacked container it is the order things come down the page; in an absolute one, the order they are drawn, each over the last. A table holds its rows here, and a row its cells, one per column.

BrushStyle.description: How an area is filled: one colour.

Color.description: Straight RGBA colour, so the engine does not depend on System.Drawing.

Constraints.description: Lower and upper bounds in millimetres on the size the resolver arrives at. Zero on a side means no bound there, so a Constraints nobody has touched changes nothing. A clamp keeps the edge the item is stuck to and moves the opposite one - and in the flow an item that states no coordinates is stuck to all four. A MaxWidth of 40 in a band of 210 therefore moves the left edge and the item lands against the right margin; a MinHeight grows the box upward, over what is already on the page. The flow cursor hears about neither, so nothing below it moves to match.

MinWidth.description: The smallest width the item may be, in millimetres; zero for no bound. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

MinHeight.description: The smallest height the item may be, in millimetres; zero for no bound. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

MaxWidth.description: The largest width the item may be, in millimetres; zero for no bound. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

MaxHeight.description: The largest height the item may be, in millimetres; zero for no bound. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

ContainerItem.description: A group of items, placed either at coordinates of their own or stacked one under the next. Everything in the model that holds children is one of these - the bands, a table and its rows, an image grid, a section.

DocumentDimension.description: The size of a sheet, in millimetres: a width and a height, with neither axis privileged - landscape is nothing more than the larger number written first. Both start at zero and nothing supplies a page size - not the engine, not the CLI, not the native library. A section that leaves them there is laid out on a sheet of nothing: /MediaBox [0 0 0 0], every column too narrow to divide, one item forced onto each page. The designer writes A4 into any section that arrives without one, which is why this is only ever met by a template built by hand.

Width.description: Width of the sheet, in millimetres - 210 for A4. Nothing supplies one: a section without a size is laid out on a sheet of nothing. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Height.description: Height of the sheet, in millimetres - 297 for A4. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

EdgeSize.description: Four distances in millimetres, one per side, serving both as the margin outside an item frame and as the padding inside it. Which of the two a band reads is settled rather than a matter of taste: the section and the body are handed their rectangle, and the resolver deflates it by their Padding without ever looking at their Margin. Page margins are a section padding; written as a margin, the same four numbers do nothing at all.

Left.description: The left side, in millimetres. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Top.description: The top side, in millimetres. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Right.description: The right side, in millimetres. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Bottom.description: The bottom side, in millimetres. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

FieldItem.description: A field the reader can fill in: the interactive half of a quote or an order form. It lays out like any other item - it has a frame, it flows, it fits in a table cell. What changes is what the backend does with it: the PDF backend writes a form widget, the SVG backend draws what it would look like. The value written here is the field's starting state, and the one drawn when the section is flattened.

$type.description: What kind of element this is.

Name.description: Name the value is stored and read back under. It must be unique in the section; a field stamped out by a repeat gets an index appended so that a prototype can be repeated without every copy answering to the same name.

Kind.description: What the reader fills in: Text, a Checkbox, or a Signature.

Value.description: Starting value. For a checkbox, anything but null, empty and "false" counts as ticked.

Tooltip.description: Shown by a reader when the pointer rests on the field.

ReadOnly.description: Shown in the form but not changeable there.

Required.description: Marked required in the form, so a reader may refuse to submit it empty.

Multiline.description: Text fields only: accept more than one line.

MaxLength.description: Text fields only: zero for no limit.

Signing.description: Signature fields only: how the section expects to be signed.

Font.description: How the value is drawn. Inherits from the section like any text.

Outline.description: Outline of the field itself. Null draws nothing, which is what you want for a field sitting on a printed rule.

Fill.description: Fill behind the field, to make it visible on a busy page.

The item is dropped - Visibility.Gone, so it takes no room and nothing beneath it moves - unless the value at that path is worth showing: present, and not an empty string, not zero, not false. Wanted the first time a form was reproduced faithfully. A box that only a credit note fills, a label for a number that is not always there, a line under an address line that may not exist: without this the choice is a rule drawn through empty space or a template per case.

HideWhen.description: The other way round: dropped when the value is there. Both may be given, and either one hiding the item is enough.

Style.description: Where the item sits and how much room it takes: position and size, margin and padding, size bounds, visibility, page breaks and alignment.

Layout.description: Always written, never inferred from its absence. The property starts at LayoutMode.Absolute, and the four containers that have to flow set themselves to LayoutMode.Stack in their constructors: Body, TableItem, ImageGridItem and SubTemplateItem. A Header, a Footer, a Section and a plain group keep the default. That matters because an absolute container hands every child the same box rather than taking room away as it goes, and a child that states no position of its own fills all of it - so two children of a band that says nothing land exactly on top of one another.

ColumnCount.description: How many columns the children flow into. One by default. Named ColumnCount rather than Columns because a table already has Columns, meaning its list of column widths - and a table is a container. Two different things under one name on the same inheritance chain is a fault waiting for somebody to write the wrong one; the compiler said so and the name changed. Only meaningful in LayoutMode.Stack: absolute children are placed by their own coordinates, and there is nothing for a column to decide.

ColumnGap.description: Millimetres between one column and the next. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

BalanceColumns.description: Whether the last page of a column flow is evened out. On by default. Columns fill in order, so the page where the text runs out has its first column full and its last nearly empty, which looks like a mistake. Balancing finds the shallowest height that still holds everything and uses that, so the columns end together. It costs a handful of extra passes over that page alone - pages that overflow have no spare room and are left as they are. Turn it off for a column of items that must start at the very top whatever happens.

RepeatOver.description: Name of the collection in the data this container repeats over, such as "Lines". The binder stamps its children out once per record; until it runs the container is an ordinary one holding the prototype. In a TableItem the header rows stay put and the remaining rows are the prototypes, cycled - two of them give banded rows for free. In any other container the whole set of children is one prototype block.

EmptyText.description: Shown in place of the children when the collection turns out empty.

GroupBy.description: Groups the collection by the value of this field before repeating, when the data arrives flat. Each pass then sees a synthetic record carrying Key, Count, a Sum of every numeric field - the subtotals - and the rows themselves under ContainerItem.GroupItems, ready for a nested repeat. Leave it null when the data is already grouped.

GroupItems.description: Name the grouped rows are published under. Defaults to "Items".

Childs.description: What this holds, in order. In a stacked container it is the order things come down the page; in an absolute one, the order they are drawn, each over the last. A table holds its rows here, and a row its cells, one per column.

Dimension.description: The sheet this section is laid out on. There is no default size, and nothing supplies one: a section that omits this lays out on a sheet of nothing - pages come out 0 by 0, every column is too narrow to divide, and the flow puts one item on each page and drops the rest, silently.

PageLimit.description: How many pages this section is *meant* to take, or null for no expectation. Purely declarative: exceeding it is reported through LayoutResult.Issues and nothing is refused. Whether to go on and produce the section belongs to whoever asked for it, which is why the engine states the fact rather than acting on it - lay out first, decide after, which Report.Resolve has always allowed. Not to be confused with LayoutResolver.MaxPages, which is a runaway guard against a layout that never converges and says so in those words.

Style.description: The box every item carries: where it sits and how big it may be, the space around it and inside it, whether it shows, what it does when the page runs out beneath it, and the rule and fill drawn on its frame. What is left unsaid is not left alone. An item with no coordinate, no width and no alignment is anchored to both edges of its band before layout begins, and comes out the full width of the column - so a one-word label given a Background paints a stripe right across the page. The item really is that wide, and nothing says so.

Location.description: Where the item sits in the space its container gives it: edges, width, height and docking.

Margin.description: Room kept outside the item's frame, in millimetres. A section's page margins are its Padding, not its Margin.

Padding.description: Room kept inside the item's frame, between its edge and its content, in millimetres. On a section, these are the page margins.

Constraints.description: Bounds on the size the engine arrives at, in millimetres.

Visibility.description: Visible; Invisible, keeping its room; or Gone, taking none.

PageBreak.description: Author-requested page break around this item. Declared, but inert until the pagination pass exists.

Splitting.description: What to do when the item does not fit in the space left on the page.

KeepWithNext.description: Do not let the page end immediately after this item.

PageScope.description: Which pages this item shows on. Declared, but inert until the pagination pass exists; PageScope.Range reads Style.PageRange.

PageRange.description: Explicit page numbers, 1-based, used when Style.PageScope is Range.

AlignHorizontal.description: Where the item sits across the space it was given. Answers the question text alignment cannot: how to centre an image, a table or a field. It applies only when the item has a width of its own and neither an anchor nor a coordinate has already placed it.

AlignVertical.description: Where the item sits down the space it was given. Only meaningful inside an absolutely arranged container: in a flow the vertical position is the cursor.

RepeatOnBreak.description: Re-emit this item at the top of the next page when the container holding it runs over. It is what a table's repeating header does, made available to any stacked container - so a group header stays above its rows when the group spills onto the following page.

Border.description: Outline stroked around the frame. Carried for the backend; the resolver ignores it.

Background.description: Fill behind the frame. Carried for the backend; the resolver ignores it.

SubTemplateItem.description: Another template brought into this one - its body spliced in where this item sits, or its sections appended after this one. Named by a path, by st://reference for the host to supply, or carried whole in TemplateData.

$type.description: What kind of element this is.

Mode.description: Whether this brings across a block or a document. See SubTemplateMode; SubTemplateMode.Splice is what this element has always done and stays the default.

TemplatePath.description: Where the other template comes from. Three shapes, and which one is used is decided by what is filled in rather than by a mode anybody has to set:

TemplateData.description: The other template's JSON, carried here rather than pointed at - so a template with sub-templates can be one file, and can be handed to something that has no file system at all. Bytes, and therefore base64 in the file, the same shape as ImageSource.Data. Which carries that type's warning: this is a byte[] and only looks like a base64 string when a template is read as JSON. Putting it in a string gives "System.Byte[]", which is valid enough to travel and draws nothing - see CLAUDE.md section 5a-bis, where that cost an afternoon on an image.

Bookmark.description: Puts an entry in the document's outline, pointing at wherever this item lands. Null for none. Tokens are filled from the data like any text, so a group heading reading {Customer.Name} gives one bookmark per customer - which is what makes a file holding two hundred invoices usable at all.

BookmarkLevel.description: How deep the entry sits: zero at the top, one nested under the last entry above it at zero, and so on. A level that skips a step is pulled back to one more than its predecessor, since an outline with a hole in it is not a tree.

Language.description: The language of this element and everything under it, as a BCP 47 tag ("de-DE", "fr"). Null - the usual case - means the file's, which is Report.Language. PDF/UA 7.2 asks that a passage in a language other than the document's be marked as such, because a reader announcing German words with English phonemes is not a cosmetic fault: it is unintelligible. It reaches the file as /Lang on this element's structure entry, which is where PDF puts it, and costs nothing when it says the same as the file.

Width.description: The column's width, in WidthUnit. Unset, the column shares with the others what the fixed ones leave. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

WidthUnit.description: Millimeter, or Percentage of the table's width.

Fit.description: Size the column to its widest cell instead of sharing the leftover space. Only meaningful when no explicit width is given.

MinWidth.description: Floor for a fitted column, in millimeters. Zero means none. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

MaxWidth.description: Ceiling for a fitted column, in millimeters. Zero means none. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

TableItem.description: A table. Its children are TableRow items, and it splits between rows when it does not fit: a row is never cut in half.

Columns.description: The columns, left to right. Every row carries one cell per column.

RepeatHeader.description: Repeat the header rows at the top of each page the table continues on.

Text.description: What is printed. Tokens in braces are filled in: {Page}, {Pages} and {Title} by the engine, a path such as {Client.Name} from the data. {{ and }} print a brace, and a line break in the string breaks the line.

Font.description: Appearance of the text, and what the resolver measures it with.

TextRun.description: One piece of an AdvancedTextItem, in the item's own base style except where TextRun.Font says otherwise. Null there means every property is inherited - the common case, a run of plain text between two styled words.

Text.description: This run's words. Tokens in braces are filled in as in a TextItem, and a line break in the string breaks the line.

Font.description: Overrides on top of the item's own AdvancedTextItem.Font, which is itself a normal cascade onto Report.DefaultFont - the same three-level resolution a plain TextItem already goes through, with one more level on top. A run does not set alignment, wrapping or line spacing: those describe the paragraph, not a piece of it.

TextStyle.description: Text appearance. TextStyle.Size is read through TextStyle.SizeUnit; the resolver converts it to points before anything measures or draws it.

Family.description: Typeface name; unset, then empty, resolves to the measurer's default family.

Size.description: Size expressed in TextStyle.SizeUnit. Defaults to 1. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Bold.description: Bold. Null inherits from the level above; a family with no bold cut is drawn in another of its cuts, never a synthesised bold.

Italic.description: Italic. Null inherits from the level above.

Underline.description: Underlined. Null inherits from the level above.

Strikethrough.description: Struck through. Null inherits from the level above.

LineSpacing.description: Distance from one baseline to the next, as a multiple of the text's own size - that is, of its cap height, the thing a size in millimetres actually pins. Defaults to 1.5. Deliberately not a multiple of the em, and deliberately not the font's own line height: both vary by half from one typeface to the next, so a table row would change height simply because the section was restyled. Here the section decides the leading and every font obeys. A face with unusually long ascenders - a script, say - needs this raised, and the page shows it at once. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Watermark.description: A word written across every page - SPECIMEN, BROUILLON, COPIE. It is drawn as ordinary page content, not as a background. That distinction is the whole point: a browser drops background graphics when printing unless the reader goes and turns them back on, so a mark drawn as a background is exactly absent from the one artefact that matters - the printout someone might pass off as an original. The engine draws it and takes no view on whether a given section needs one.

Text.description: DRAFT rather than SPECIMEN. Both are marks, and the repository's samples had said DRAFT since the day the watermark folder was made to name its modes rather than its words - while this line went on proposing the other one, so a mark made in the designer never matched a mark made anywhere else.

Mode.description: Tiled across the whole sheet, or written once (Single).

Layer.description: In front by default. Behind, the mark is at the mercy of whatever the content paints over it: a filled title bar or a shaded table header erases it exactly there, which is the failure every report library has - and it clears the areas worth tampering with. In front it is translucent instead, so both stay legible.

Angle.description: Degrees anticlockwise from horizontal. 45 by default: a diagonal crosses both the lines of text and the rules of a table, so no part of the page is left with a clean horizontal band to work in. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

Font.description: How the word is drawn. Its size is a cap height in millimetres like any other text, so the mark scales with the section rather than with the paper. Mid grey at thirty percent on purpose: it shifts white paper and a black title bar by the same amount, so the mark reads over both. A light grey looks better on white and vanishes on anything dark - which is where it is needed.

Spacing.description: Millimetres between one copy and the next, along the diagonal and across it. Ignored in WatermarkMode.Single. Zero means "from the text": a gap of half the word's own length, which stays right whatever the size. A number; the string "NaN" means undecided.

PageScope.description: Pages that carry the mark. All of them, unless narrowed.
